<!-- generated by scripts/gen_doc_tables.py from src/lib/figure.F90 and the modules' doc comments: do not edit -->
| Module | What it holds |
|---|---|
| `figure_app` | the application: window, frame loop and lazy redraw. |
| `figure_base` | error handling and string conversion shared by the FIGURE modules. |
| `figure_canvas` | an area that takes the mouse and drawing primitives: the way to build a widget FIGURE does not have. |
| `figure_dock` | docking: windows docked into one another or into a dock space, and layouts set by the program. |
| `figure_editor` | a code editor (code_editor_object) with highlighting, marks, completion and find, and a text diff. |
| `figure_files` | files and folders: make, remove, time, test, the same on every platform. |
| `figure_group` | widgets that group other widgets: child regions, headers, tabs, tables, trees, id scopes, disabled blocks, |
| `figure_imgui` | Dear ImGui widgets with Fortran arguments. |
| `figure_implot` | ImPlot plots with Fortran arrays. |
| `figure_implot3d` | small 3-D figures with Fortran arrays (ImPlot3D). |
| `figure_markdown` | Markdown in the window: a text at the cursor (ig_markdown) and documents (markdown_view_object). |
| `figure_menu` | menus, popups and keyboard shortcuts. |
| `figure_numbers` | numbers and choices: fields, drag boxes and sliders for integers and reals, scalar or vector; angles; |
| `figure_player` | a player for snapshots: previous, play, next, a slider, a speed and a loop mode. |
| `figure_process` | programs started from the program (process_object) and a view of their output (log_view_object). |
| `figure_style` | every colour and variable of the Dear ImGui and ImPlot styles, by name. |
| `figure_task` | background tasks: Fortran procedures run on a worker thread, with progress and cooperative cancel. |
| `figure_texture` | RGBA images on the GPU, drawn by `ig_image` and `ip_image`, and PNG or JPEG files read into pixels. |
| `figure_view3d` | a 3-D view of meshes (view3d_object), drawn by FIGURE's software rasterizer in every mode. |
| `figure_testing` | synthetic input for testing interfaces without a display (or with one). (`use figure_testing`, apart from `figure`) |
